_comment: Terms DeepL has no business guessing at. Resolved BEFORE the API is called, so DeepL
never sees them and cannot mangle them.
keep   Strings that pass through UNCHANGED in every target language. Brand names,
book titles, proper nouns, Sanskrit terms. Matched on the exact trimmed string.
terms  Per-target-language overrides, keyed by DeepL target code (EN-GB, DE, CS, ...).
keepInline  Names that must survive UNCHANGED even when they appear INSIDE a longer
sentence, not just as the whole string. Sent to DeepL wrapped in an ignore_tags
marker, so the prose around them still translates and reorders normally.
This is deliberately NARROWER than `keep`. `keep` holds Prague and Praha, which
are correct as whole-string labels but must NOT be frozen mid-sentence: Czech
prose should say Praha and Russian should say Прага. Only names with no correct
localisation at all belong here — the brand above all, which came back from
DeepL as Гульдар-Базар on 24 Aug 2026 and started this list.
Matched on the exact trimmed source string.
The EN-GB block came from vendors/govinda/data/glossary.json (Czech transliterations of
Sanskrit, which machine translation reads as Czech words and returns nonsense for). It is
shared now: both the Govinda vendor pipeline and the site translation pass read this file.
Adding an entry costs nothing and saves a character of quota every time the term recurs.

4 Sep 2026: the /partner instrument names were added to keepInline — GPSR, REACH, EORI, IOSS, TARIC, EPR, RoDTEP, IEC, LUT, e-BRC, DGFT, EDPMS. Those name specific legal acts and a paraphrase of one describes a role instead of naming it. The page is machine-translated from this date by an explicit decision that overrode the 3 Sep English-only rule.

What is NOT frozen, and why the first attempt had to be undone: VAT, GST, IGST, RRP, FOB and Responsible Person are common nouns or have official translations in the regulation's own language versions. Freezing them produced 'EU-VATn' in German and "l'VATs de l'UE" in French — an English noun cannot take a German plural or a French elision. GPSR itself is published in every EU language, so 'verantwortliche Person' and 'personne responsable' ARE the legal terms, not paraphrases of one.

EN-GB.Návraty: Coming Back: The Science of Reincarnation
